column.text: Bitcoin is currently trading above seventy-two thousand dollars, having just triggered a historic short squeeze that wiped out over four hundred and forty-six million dollars in leveraged positions. This massive liquidation event confirms the market's aggressive bullish bias as institutional capital pours into spot ETFs at a record pace of five-hundred-and-seventeen-million dollars within twenty-four hours. The decoupling from traditional equities is undeniable, with Bitcoin showing near-zero correlation to the Nasdaq while tech giants like Nvidia and Microsoft flatline or decline. This divergence signals that crypto-native momentum has completely overridden macroeconomic noise regarding interest rates or national debt concerns. However, traders must recognize that extreme overbought conditions are now flashing warning lights across major assets, specifically Ethereum which sits at an RSI reading of ninety-four on the four-hour chart and XRP hovering near eighty-nine. These technical extremes suggest imminent mean reversion is likely before any further continuation can occur. The tape remains up-trending with a risk-on regime where momentum longs still carry tailwinds, but shorts require genuine catalysts like supply unlocks or failed breakouts rather than simple exhaustion fades to be valid. Liquidity context dictates that dollar supplies are contracting against these surging assets, demanding higher proof of life for any new long entries while treating stalled rallies as superior short opportunities. The narrative is shifting from pure speculation to a regime where institutional demand meets aggressive retail leverage in an environment devoid of traditional safe havens.
